BCA, checked one component at a time

Bayesian Conformal Aggregation (BCA) is the project's method for putting an error band around an offline critic and turning that band into caution for the actor. This page verifies it on the ThrusterChain test bed (a simulated boat with four thrusters) module by module, in the order data flow through the method. Written 20 October 2026 from the code at commit 52914e4 of the repository and from its committed records. Nothing was trained for it. Every number below is printed by a script in docs/bca_mechanics/scripts/ or quoted from a module page in docs/bca_mechanics/modules/, which names the record. The verdict words are only: works, works with a caveat, does not work, untested. Evidence labels: pre-registered (the rule was frozen before the run), exploratory (designed after seeing the data, or outside a pre-registration), description only (what the code does; no claim about a result).

The summary in ten lines.

  1. Overall verdict: works with a caveat. The arithmetic from recorded rows to the band (M1 to M6) works and reproduces every stored number bit for bit; the three uses that read the band's width (M7, M8, M9) do not move the actor where it matters; the one use that works (M10, M11) reads held-out outcomes, and its height is undefined for small groups.
  2. Module verdicts: M1 works; M2 works with a caveat; M3 works; M4 works with a caveat; M5 works; M6 works with a caveat; M7 works with a caveat; M8 does not work; M9 does not work; M10 works with a caveat; M11 works with a caveat. Nothing is untested.
  3. Takeaway 1. The mechanics are right. Recomputed from the saved networks in the pinned environment, every stored score, threshold and width comes back exactly (10 of 10 near-80 bands in M1; 25 of 25 bands in M3; 30 of 30 thresholds in M5; 40 of 40 certificates in M10). Weights of 1 give the standard band to the last bit (W0 25 of 25; S2; 30 of 30 recomputed banks).
  4. Takeaway 2. The band describes the recorded rows, not the critic's error where the data stop. It covers 0.90 to 0.94 of fresh rows from the recorded situations in 20 of 20 bands, but it is a band on the critic's one-step target, it holds on average over rows (0.94 at low current, 0.87 at high), and in the stalling world it covers only half of the removed commands. The error-size network is nearly a constant (replacing it by its average lowers coverage by under one point), so the width is flat across commands and the dose (1.29 to 1.39 everywhere) and the lower edge (0.1 to 0.5% of the critic's over-optimism) cannot steer the actor.
  5. Takeaway 3. The penalty is low under IID and higher under a shift only when the shift is declared. Standard BCA's penalty is the same number under IID and shifted tests (it never looks at the test condition); what drops under a shift is coverage, 0.89-0.94 to 0.80-0.87 on 25 of 25 seeds. Importance-weighted BCA equals standard BCA bit for bit when the weights are 1; with weights for a declared shift its threshold is 1.11 to 2.25 times higher on 25 of 25 seeds, by construction. The two exceptions are classifier-estimated weights (noise of about plus or minus 5%, 14 seeds up, 9 down) and refusal when the effective group has fewer than about 29 rows (8 of 40 certificates).
  6. The one BCA component that points the right way is the harm switch: on in 20 of 20 stalling worlds, off in 20 of 20 no-stall worlds, because it reads held-out outcomes of the full-throttle group rather than the band's width.
  7. Its weak point: the height it hands to the ramp is a difference of two credible thresholds, infinite whenever the full-throttle group holds fewer than about 29 rows; that stopped 3 of 5 fresh stalling seeds of the pre-registered confirmation (claim 4 failed by rule).
  8. Where the records measure the truth separately, the critic is 2.27 times as wrong where data are missing (the gate's harm check); the one-step residual that every module stands on cannot see that part (an error shared by a row and its next step is shrunk by 1 minus 0.98 = 0.02).
  9. Consistent cases are the rule: every test below reports the same pattern on every seed and both worlds. The exceptional cases are few, named, and each has a reproduction command.
  10. How to read on: the pipeline, then one section per module, then the penalty evidence, then what this does and does not show, then a glossary.

Two words used throughout. The critic is the host's learned estimate q of how much return a command earns from a state; the host is TD3+BC, an offline reinforcement-learning algorithm, in every ThrusterChain study. The held-out rows are recorded steps kept out of training for calibration (about 800 to 850 per band; the code calls them "the bank"). The pinned environment is Python 3.10.20, NumPy 2.2.6 and JAX 0.6.2 on CPU, the versions the studies ran under; it is needed whenever a recomputed number must equal a recorded one to the last bit. The near-80 run, stage 2, step 1 and step 2, the weighting test and the four-learner study are the recorded studies; the glossary at the end defines each.

M1. The residual works

What it does. The residual is the critic's own one-step training error at a recorded row: the host's target y (the reward plus the discounted value the target copies of the critic give the next state under the target actor's command, with clipped noise on that command) minus the critic's value q at the recorded command. BCA computes it on every training batch (for M2) and once per refresh on every held-out row (for M3).

0[M1.0 rows and key]   at every update: the 256-row training batch, noise key fold_in(step key, 1179210836);
                           at a refresh: EVERY held-out row, noise key fold_in(refresh key, 1213156420)
1[M1.1 target noise]   eps = clip(Normal(0, 0.2^2), -0.5, 0.5), one draw per row AND per thruster (rows x 4)
2[M1.2 next command]   a' = clip(target_actor(s') + eps, -1, 1)
3[M1.3 target]         y = r + 0.98 (1 - d) min(targetQ1(s', a'), targetQ2(s', a')); held constant (stop_gradient)
4[M1.4 critic value]   q = min(Q1(s, a), Q2(s, a)) at the RECORDED command a, from the ONLINE critic
5[M1.5 residual]       e = y - q  (line 197 feeds its SD to the unit, M2.7; line 267 passes it to the scores, M3)

The test. M1_test.py calls the repository's own native_target and td3_bc_update on random networks and 512 random rows: y equals the written formula to 1.1e-7, rows with d = 1 give y = r exactly, and the host's critic loss under the same key equals the loss built from BCA's y (1.864258 against 1.864258; under another key 1.865237, so the equality is not trivial). On a self-loop world whose exact value is s/(1 − 0.98), an exact critic gives residual 0 (largest 3.8e-6), a critic too high by b everywhere gives −0.02 b, too high only at the recorded rows gives −b, and only at the next step +0.98 b. Then M1_real.py, in the pinned environment, regenerates each near-80 log through the gate's loader (row hashes equal the band records, 10 of 10), loads the saved critic and band (SHA-256 checked), recomputes y, q and e at every held-out row with the refresh's own key, and carries e downstream: the scores equal the stored arrays byte for byte and the threshold equals the stored R in all 10 bands.

On the held-out rows the residual's median size is 0.10 return units against critic values of −8 to −54, and large residuals are about twice as common in the high-current third as in the low-current third in 10 of 10 bands (table R3).

Verdict: works. The residual is the critic's own one-step training error at a recorded row; recomputed from the saved critics it reproduces every stored score and threshold, but it measures the critic's consistency with itself, not its error against the truth.

Reproduce it

set PYTHONPATH=M:\        (the repository root)
set JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu
python docs\bca_mechanics\scripts\M1_test.py
pwsh -NoProfile -File <scratchpad>\wslrun.ps1 -ScriptFile M:\docs\bca_mechanics\scripts\M1_real.sh -TimeoutSec 900 -Name m1real

The first command prints tables S1-S4 and R1-R3 and writes the figure (about 10 s; Windows venv). The second runs the pinned-environment recomputation through the WSL bridge (138 s for ten bands); its output is committed as data/M1/M1_real_results.json.

M2. The error-size network and the unit works with a caveat

What it does. The error-size network η(s, a) is a small network (two layers of 64 units) that predicts, per row, how large the residual should be, as a multiple of the unit u, a running average of the residual's spread in critic value units. Both are fitted so that about 90% of residuals satisfy |e| ≤ u·η, with a loss that trades a little coverage for a narrower band.

0[M2.0 data normalization] the data pipeline normalizes every state by the kept training rows' mean and SD (+0.001)
1[M2.1 inputs]        x = concat(s_normalized / 1.001, a)
2[M2.2 network]       h = ReLU(W1 x); h = ReLU(W2 h); eta = softplus(w3 . h) + 0.01     (eta >= 0.01)
3[M2.3 masses]        E_i ~ Exponential(1) for the 256 rows; m_i = E_i / sum_j E_j   (a Bayesian-bootstrap draw)
4[M2.4 soft coverage] c_i = sigmoid(20 (y_i/u - (q_i/u - eta_i))) * sigmoid(20 ((q_i/u + eta_i) - y_i/u))
5[M2.5 loss]          L = (sum_i m_i c_i - 0.9)^2 + 0.005 * sum_i m_i eta_i^2   (its minimum sits at coverage 0.87)
6[M2.6 step]          one Adam step (learning rate 0.001) on eta's parameters only; y, q and u are constants
7[M2.7 unit]          u_new = 0.99 u + 0.01 max(SD_batch(y - q), 1e-6)
8[M2.8 accept]        keep the new parameters and u_new only if every number is finite, eta > 0, the masses
                       sum to 1, u > 0 and u_new > 0; otherwise keep the old ones

algorithms/td3_bc_bca.py:159-231 (fit_scale; masses 175-177, loss 184-188, accept 199-227), :132-137 (construction); calibration/network.py:16-31 (the network), 34-37 (soft coverage), 44-46 (masses); experiments/shift/learners.py:193-197, 251-262 (the normalization)

The test. M2_test.py drives the real fit_scale on 40,000 synthetic rows whose error size is known (visible to the network, constant, or hidden), 20,000 steps of 256 rows: every step accepted, η finite and above its floor, the unit within 3% of the residual's spread, and the share inside u·η on the rows the fit saw 0.878-0.886, the loss's own equilibrium of 0.870. Where the size is visible η follows it (rank correlation 0.880); where it is hidden η is flat and the band is wrong row by row (1.00 on the smallest-error tenth, 0.43 on the largest) while the average stays 0.833: the fit enforces coverage on average, never row by row. On the 20 recorded ThrusterChain bands (M2_pinned.py, pinned environment): all 400,000 fit steps accepted; η and the scores equal the stored arrays byte for byte; on the training rows the share inside u·η is 0.867-0.891; on the held-out rows 0.762-0.827, because the critic's errors on rows it never trained on are 1.20-1.60 times larger (the threshold of M5 absorbs that: R 1.35-1.71). Replacing η by one number lowers held-out coverage by under one point; from the weakest to the strongest tenth of the current the critic's error grows 82% and η grows 7%.

M3. The scores works

What it does. At a refresh BCA freezes η and u and turns each held-out residual into a score: the actual error divided by the predicted error size, ρ = |y − q| / (u·max(η, 1e-6)). A score of 1 means the critic's error was exactly as large as predicted; the scores are dimensionless, so rows with different predicted sizes share one scale.

1[M3.1 freeze]      eta_f, u_f = the calibrator's current parameters and the current unit at the refresh
2[M3.2 inputs]      on the held-out rows: y_j with the refresh key (module M1), q_j = min of the two heads, eta_j = eta_f(s_j, a_j)
3[M3.3 pre-check]   the host refuses the refresh (keeps the previous reference) unless the state, rows, y, q and every eta_j are finite
4[M3.4 scale]       sigma_j = max(eta_j, 1e-6) * u_f, computed in float32, then converted to float64
5[M3.5 validity]    require: parameters finite; u_f finite and > 0; every sigma_j finite and > 0; every residual finite
6[M3.6 score]       rho_j = |y_j - q_j| / sigma_j in float64
7[M3.7 hand-off]    rho_1..rho_n go to M5 (wbcp.calibrate) with the stream seeded from fold_in(refresh key, 1347375956)
8[M3.8 after M5]    a finite threshold that overflows float32 also invalidates the refresh; else R, lambda_hat, lambda_HPD, n_eff are stored in float32

The test. On 2,000 synthetic rows with a made-up η, u = 0.37 and residuals u·η·Z (Z standard normal) the real functions give scores equal to |Z| (largest relative difference 5.7e-08), only the product u·η matters (bit for bit), the 1e-6 floor changes 0 of 2,000 rows, invalid inputs are refused rather than scored, and weights of 1 give the unweighted threshold bit for bit. On all 25 recorded frozen-critic bands (10 near-80, 15 stage 2) the stored score array's SHA-256 equals the record, the plain 90% quantile recomputed as the ceil(0.9 n)-th smallest score equals the recorded one, and wbcp.calibrate with the refresh's own stream gives the recorded R, λ̂, λ_HPD and n_eff in float32 on 25 of 25. In the pinned environment (M3_recompute_pinned.py) the scores and η recompute from the saved critic and band through the study's own function, bit for bit, on 20 of 20 bands whose critic the near-80 code can load.

The scores are larger in the high-current third on 20 of 20 bands: a band calibrated to miss 10% of all held-out rows misses about 12% of the high-current rows and 5-7% of the others. Weights never touch this step; they only make those rows count more in M5. Verdict: works. The score step is one line of arithmetic with no free choice; it reproduces every stored number exactly, so a fault in BCA lies in what the network predicts (M2) or how the threshold is chosen (M5), not here.

M4. The weights works with a caveat

What it does. A weight w_j says how much held-out row j counts: how often its situation occurs at test time divided by how often it occurred in training (a ratio of densities of the water current c); the test mass t is the weight of the row being certified. Standard BCA uses w_j = 1 and t = 1; the weighting test used exact weights from known laws and estimated weights from a logistic classifier that separates test observations from training observations.

0[M4.0 validation]  weights without t, or t without weights, are refused; weights finite and >= 0; t finite and > 0
1[M4.1 standard]    w_j = 1 for every held-out row; t = 1 (the default when no weights are passed)
2[M4.2 exact]       w_j = p_test(c_j) / p_train(c_j) from the known laws of the current; per step: t = w(c_step);
                     single method: one t = E_test[w] for every step
3[M4.3 estimated]   logistic regression (training sample = 0, test sample = 1) on the 13-number observation, Newton,
                     no penalty; w_j = exp(log-odds(x_j)) * n0 / n1; a step's t likewise at its observation
4[M4.4 support]     a test step whose command lies inside the removed ball: ratio +infinity, refused before M5
5[M4.5 scale]       divide every w_j and t by max_j w_j (only ratios matter)
6[M4.6 size]        n_eff = (sum_j w_j)^2 / sum_j w_j^2   (the Kish effective size)

calibration/wbcp.py:66-85, 116; experiments/shift_iw/world.py:128-164; experiments/shift_iw/classifier.py:38-46, 69-117; experiments/shift_iw/coverage.py:78-97, 251-259; experiments/shift_iw/run.py:549-607; experiments/shift_iw/data.py:712

The test. M4_test.py checks the exact-weight formula against the specification's constants (test masses 1.0000, 1.3811, 2.8415; Kish rows of 1,000: 1000, 724, 352 for no shift, mild, strong), that weights of 1 reproduce the unweighted threshold and all 1,000 crossings bit for bit on 42 of 42 synthetic held-out sets, that a common factor changes nothing (36 of 36), that the classifier recovers slopes 0, 2 and 4 (independent rows within 0.02), and that under a synthetic strong shift the plain weighted quantile alone brings coverage from 0.792 back to 0.902 (the full threshold 0.818 to 0.940). On the 10 recorded near-80 bands (M4_pinned.py, pinned environment) weights of 1 are identical on 10 of 10, exact weights for a declared tilt of the recorded current raise the threshold by 2-11% (slope 2) and 4-41% (slope 4), the classifier fitted on recorded observations gives slopes 2.008 ± 0.048 and 4.010 ± 0.028 (−0.017 ± 0.072 with no tilt), and refusal is exactly inside the ball (1.00 inside, 0.00 outside, on 30,000 evaluation rows per band).

Where the weights were estimated for the actor's own command law instead of a tilt of the current, the held-out set was worth 2-156 effective rows of about 850, and the band refused rather than certified.

Verdict: works with a caveat. With weights of 1 weighted BCA is standard BCA to the last bit, and weights for a known shift do their job; but every weight on record comes from a shift law we know, and weights for the actor's own commands collapse to a handful of effective rows.

Reproduce it

set PYTHONPATH=M:\
python docs\bca_mechanics\scripts\M4_test.py                                   (a few minutes; --fast for a quick run)
pwsh -NoProfile -File <scratchpad>\wslrun.ps1 -ScriptFile M:\docs\bca_mechanics\scripts\M4_pinned_job.sh -TimeoutSec 1500 -Name m4pinned

The pinned job writes data/M4_real_data.json (about 2 minutes); the test script prints its table from that file.

M5. The threshold, with refusal works

What it does. From the list of held-out scores, M5 returns the threshold R: the score below which 90% of fresh scores should fall, with 95% credibility, as the larger of a plain (weighted) 90% quantile and the 950th smallest of 1,000 random reweightings ("draws") that each include one extra test atom standing for the unseen row. R = +infinity is a refusal ("cannot certify"); with equal weights it happens exactly when fewer than 950 draws cross, and a draw crosses with probability 1 − 0.9^n, so refusal depends on the group size n alone.

1[M5.1 sort]           sort the scores ascending; carry the weights along; divide weights and t by max w
2[M5.2 plain quantile] lambda_hat = the smallest sorted score at which the cumulative weight >= 0.9 * total weight
3[M5.3 draws]          for m = 1..1000: E_1..E_n, E_{n+1} ~ Exponential(1) from numpy's default_rng seeded by fold_in(refresh key, 1347375956)
4[M5.4 crossing]       lambda^(m) = the first sorted score k with sum_{j<=k} E_j w_j >= 0.9 (sum_j E_j w_j + E_{n+1} t);
                        +infinity if no k reaches it (the test atom alone holds more than 10% of the mass)
5[M5.5 credible]       lambda_HPD = the 950th smallest of the 1,000 crossings
6[M5.6 threshold]      R = max(lambda_hat, lambda_HPD); R = +infinity means refusal ("cannot certify")
7[M5.7 store]          store R, lambda_hat, lambda_HPD, n_eff in float32; a finite R that overflows float32 makes the refresh invalid
8[M5.8 schedule]       co-training: refresh at update 10,000, then every 5,000 (18 refreshes); frozen critic: 20,000 fit steps, one refresh
9[M5.9 per-step table] with weights: R(t) on the grid t = 1.01^k, the same stream for every t; a step reads R at the smallest grid mass >= its own
10[M5.10 certificate]  the harm switch: the same calibrate twice, on the full-throttle group and on the rest; R_tail - R_rest is the height

M6. The band works with a caveat

What it does. The band at any state and command is q ± U with half-width U(s, a) = R · u_f · max(η_f(s, a), 1e-6), from the frozen η, u and the threshold R; a row is covered when its target y lies inside. Coverage of a group of rows is the share covered, with refused rows counting against it.

0[M6.0 inputs]      R, u_f and eta_f's parameters are the ones frozen at the LAST refresh; every readout uses them unchanged
1[M6.1 width]       U(s, a) = R * (max(eta_f(s, a), 1e-6) * u_f)      float32 (stage 2 and near-80 multiply (R * u_f) * eta: up to 5 float32 steps apart)
2[M6.2 not ready]   before the first refresh: U = 0 everywhere and the dose is 1
3[M6.3 refusal]     R = +infinity: U = +infinity; the row is unsupported (stage 2 and near-80 substitute U_max, the largest finite width)
4[M6.4 covered]     a row is covered when q - U <= y <= q + U; a refused row is marked -1 and never covered
5[M6.5 coverage]    coverage of a group = covered rows / all rows; 95% interval by resampling whole episodes 2,000 times
6[M6.6 where read]  at the recorded (s, a) of held-out or test rows (this module), at kept training rows (M7), at the actor's own command (M9)

M7. The dose on the behavior-cloning term works with a caveat

What it does. TD3+BC's actor loss has a behavior-cloning term, the squared distance between the actor's command and the recorded command at each training row. The dose is a per-row multiplier on that term, m = 1 + 0.5·U/(U + u), larger where the band is wide relative to the unit, read at the recorded row and never at the actor's own command.

1[M7.1 readout point]  read eta_f at the RECORDED row (s_i, a_i), not at the actor's command
2[M7.2 width]          U_i = R * u_f * max(eta_f(s_i, a_i), 1e-6)
3[M7.3 dose]           m_i = 1 + 0.5 * U_i / (U_i + u_f)   (float32; a normalized ratio, so it cannot overflow)
4[M7.4 refusal]        R = +infinity: standard BCA gives m_i = 1; the weighting test's per-row arm and the four-learner weighted setups give 1.5
5[M7.5 not ready]      before the first refresh: U_i = 0 and m_i = 1 on every row
6[M7.6 use]            every 2nd update: loss = -lambda * mean_i Q1(s_i, pi(s_i)) + mean_i m_i * mean_j (pi(s_i)_j - a_ij)^2,
                        lambda = alpha / mean_i |Q1(s_i, pi(s_i))| (detached, recomputed every actor update); m is detached
7[M7.7 per-row]        with weights: m_i uses the row's own threshold R(w_i) from the per-step table (M5.9)
8[M7.8 validity]       if any input is not finite, the whole update is discarded; a bad input is never dosed silently

The formula of calibration/dose.py is called on 3,602 widths from 0 to 10^30 units: m(0) = 1, 1 ≤ m ≤ 1.5 everywhere, the largest gap to the closed form 9.2e-8, 0 falls of the dose as the width rises over 100,000 sorted widths, dose 1 before the first refresh and on refused rows under the standard rule, 1.5 under the per-row rule, and the per-row dose with one threshold equals frozen_level_dose byte for byte. On the 20 recorded near-80 bands the dose at the 824,276 recorded training rows (pinned environment) has mean 1.307 to 1.341, every value in [1, 1.5), largest fall 1.19e-7 (one float32 step), 0 refused rows. The weighting test's pre-registered mark WT-M3 passed on all five qualities (largest fall 1.19e-7, bar 1e-6); its mark R2 found strong-shift weights raise the mean dose by only +0.018 to +0.053, predicting a return change of +0.42 and +0.92 points where 1.8 was needed, so BCA's training arms never ran. Section 6 of modules/M7.md. The slope of the dose in ln U is at most 0.125 and falling, so even a 1.2-1.8 times threshold change moves the dose by a few hundredths; within a batch the dose varies by only 0.007-0.013 (standard deviation), so it acts as a nearly constant extra pull of 1.33 rather than as row-by-row caution.

Verdict: works with a caveat. The dose is computed exactly as specified and behaves exactly as specified on every recorded row, standard and weighted, but it is nearly a constant 1.33: it saturates, so weighting moves it by only 0.02 to 0.15 and no study has shown that it raises return.

M8. The width penalty on critic values (toy worlds only) does not work

What it does. At every decision, subtract the band's half-width from the critic's value and take the action with the best remainder, a* = argmax_a [q − U]. It was tested only in a two-step, two-context toy world (bca_channel_toy.ipynb) where one decision cell, the gap, has no recorded ventures, and its kill rule was written and fingerprinted before the run.

0[M8.0 scores]      score of a held-out row = |y - q(t, c, a)| / scale(t, c, a); scale = the cell's residual SD shrunk toward the step's pooled SD
1[M8.1 threshold]   r_t = the exact BCA threshold on the held-out scores of step t (the infinitely-many-draws binomial form)
2[M8.2 width]       U(t, c, a) = r_t * scale(t, c, a)          (no error-size network: a per-cell SD; the gap cell gets the pooled SD)
3[M8.3 penalty]     at EVERY decision cell: choose a = argmax_a [ q(t, c, a) - 1.0 * U(t, c, a) ]
4[M8.4 variant A2]  the same U inside M7's dose in a discrete behavior-cloning actor
5[M8.5 judged by]   pooled regret against the kill rule: close at least a quarter of the room (pooled regret at most 0.0911)

M9. The lower edge does not work

What it does. In every actor update the lower edge adds a penalty equal to how much wider BCA's band is at the actor's own command than at the recorded command of the same state, kept where positive, and the actor climbs Q1 − k·W instead of Q1 (k = 1). The gradient reaches the actor only through the error-size network's command input.

M10. The harm switch certificate works with a caveat

What it does. The harm switch decides, per seed and world, whether a second critic (trained without the full-throttle survivors) is credibly more over-optimistic on the full-throttle group than on the rest, by running M5's posterior on each group's one-sided overestimates and reading the 5% quantile of the difference of their crossings; on when that quantile exceeds a margin of 0.10. It also hands on a height, the difference of the two groups' thresholds, which M11 turns into a penalty.

1[M10.1 throttle index]   t(a) = max over the four thrusters of |a_k|   (no error-size network anywhere in M10)
2[M10.2 gap rule]         among the kept training rows' t's strictly above their 99th percentile, the largest gap between
                           neighbors gives t_lo and t_up; defined iff t_up - t_lo >= 0.05 and >= 9 rows have t > t_lo (the survivors)
3[M10.3 second critic]    train the same fixed-controller critic on the kept rows MINUS the survivors (100,000 updates)
4[M10.4 overestimate]     s = min(Q1,Q2)(o, a) - [r + 0.98 (1 - d) min(Q1,Q2)(o', c(o'))], c = the stall-aware controller, no noise
5[M10.5 groups]           tail = survivors + held-out rows with t > t_lo;  rest = held-out rows with t <= t_lo
6[M10.6 posteriors]       BCA's posterior (M5.3-M5.4, weights 1) on each group, streams [20261015, 9700, seed, world, 1] and [..., 2]
7[M10.7 statistic]        q05 = the 5% quantile of (tail crossing - rest crossing) over all 1,000 x 1,000 pairs
8[M10.8 switch]           on iff q05 > 0.10 value units
9[M10.9 height]           h = R_tail - R_rest; h = +infinity when the tail cannot be certified (fewer than 950 finite crossings)
10[M10.10 shuffle control] permute the pooled scores between the groups and recompute with the same streams (step 1's record only)

outputs/shift/beyond-the-data/restructure/step1/step1lib.py:174-176, 179-206, 216-221, 226-234, 237-241, 244-276 (switch 267, height 271), 290-305; near80/code/learner_phases.py:98-236; near80_constants.py:109-111

The test. On two synthetic groups whose 90% quantiles differ by a known gap (40 and 830 rows, spread 0.15 as in the records), q05 is a lower bound on the true gap in 90-96% of data sets, the switch never fires with no gap (0 of 1,800 sets), fires in 6% of sets when the gap equals the margin and always from a gap of 0.30; with a clear gap and a small group the switch is on at every size while the height is finite exactly as often as the binomial rule predicts (0 at 25 rows, 0.705 at 29, 1 at 33). The 40 recorded certificates (30 near-80, 10 step 1): on in 20 of 20 stalling worlds (q05 0.559-1.263), off in 20 of 20 no-stall worlds (−0.047 to 0.053), the margin 0.10 between them. M10_recompute_pinned.py reran the gap rule, the saved second critic and the certificate for all 30 near-80 seed-worlds: every numeric field equals the record (30 of 30), and the per-row scores recompute the certificate on this machine with a largest difference of 0.0. Shuffling the pooled scores 200 times per seed-world switched it on in 9 of 6,000 permutations; 20 other random streams never changed the decision (30 of 30) but moved a finite height by up to a factor of two (seed 1, near-80 setting: 2.56 recorded, 2.56-4.87).

Where finite, R_tail is the tail's largest score in 13 of 23 seed-worlds and its second largest in 10, so the height is the gap between one or two extreme overestimates and the rest's ordinary 90% level; in the harmless world it is 0.04-0.78, not zero. The full-throttle group is the survivors (0-3 held-out rows join it); its size, 18-60 rows, is set by the data, not by BCA.

Verdict: works with a caveat. The harm switch was right in 40 of 40 seed-worlds and reproduces to the digit; its height is undefined below about 29 full-throttle rows (3 of 5 fresh stalling seeds) and, where finite, rests on one or two extreme scores.

Reproduce it

set PYTHONPATH=M:\
python docs\bca_mechanics\scripts\M10_test.py              (about 410 s; --fast for a fifth of the repetitions; --figure-only redraws)
python docs\bca_mechanics\scripts\certificate_table.py     (standard library: the 40 rows and the three recorded stops)
pwsh -NoProfile -File <scratchpad>\wslrun.ps1 -ScriptFile docs\bca_mechanics\scripts\M10_recompute_job.sh -TimeoutSec 1800

The pinned job writes data/M10/recomputed_certificates.json and data/M10/overestimates.npz (about 90 s per setting); the test script reads them, so it needs neither WSL nor JAX.

M11. The ramp height works with a caveat

What it does. When the switch is on, the actor is charged a penalty on throttle: zero up to where the recorded throttles stop (t_lo), rising in a straight line across the empty stretch to the certificate's height h at t_up, flat beyond; charged only for climbing further up the ramp than the recorded command did. With the switch off, h = 0 and the actor is the no-caution actor.

1[M11.1 ramp]            ramp(t) = clip((t - t_lo) / (t_up - t_lo), 0, 1)
2[M11.2 surface]         U(a) = h * ramp(t(a)), t(a) = max_k |a_k|; h = the certificate's height when the switch is on, else 0
3[M11.3 paired penalty]  P_i = k * max(U(pi(s_i)) - U(a_i), 0), k = 1 (k = 2 for the dose arm)
4[M11.4 actor loss]      -lambda * mean_i [Q1(s_i, pi(s_i)) - P_i] + mean_i mean_j (pi(s_i)_j - a_ij)^2, lambda = 5 / stopgrad(mean_i |Q1|);
                          Adam 3e-4, batches of 256, 20,000 steps in chunks of 4,000 from the cloned actor
5[M11.5 h = 0]           the penalty and its gradient are exactly 0: the arm must equal the no-caution actor within 1e-5
6[M11.6 refusal]         a switched-on arm with h = +infinity is refused: that seed-world's actor phase stops (both worlds of the seed)
7[M11.7 rivals]          always-on ramp at the stalling world's h; fixed h = 1.0; the plain 90%-quantile gap; the mean gap; the ramp from the knee

outputs/shift/beyond-the-data/restructure/step2/step2lib.py:383-401 (ramp, surface, penalty), 315-364 (arm table; refusal 355-359); step2/machinery.py:121-135 (the actor loss); near80/code/policy_phase.py:97-153; near80_constants.py:104-114

The test. On step2lib's own functions: the ramp is 0 up to t_lo, linear to 1 at t_up and flat after (1,201 grid points); the charge is never negative, never above k·h, 0 wherever the actor's throttle is at or below the recorded one; at h = 0 the penalty and its gradient are exactly 0 (NumPy and JAX); the arm table built from the switch records reproduces every locked arm row (178 of 178) and the three fresh-seed stops with their recorded message. The recorded height-0 checks against the no-caution actor are 0.0 in 104 of 104 arms, and 70 of 70 recomputed from the saved actors in the pinned environment. On recorded training rows the no-caution actor would pay 0.11-0.51 value units under BCA's ramp (it climbs past t_lo in 10-17% of states); the trained ramp actor pays 0.0006-0.0032 and stays below t_lo in 96.5-99.6% of states; in the 12 no-stall seed-worlds the penalty is exactly 0. Three one-state toys with a known truth show that an outcome can only say a height is "large enough" unless the critic is curved and the ramp starts below the harm.

Verdict: works with a caveat. The ramp is plumbed correctly and the switched ramp earned 100 points or more in every stalling seed-world while leaving the no-stall worlds untouched; but the outcome is flat across heights from 1.5 to 12, so BCA's height is large enough, not shown calibrated, and 3 of 5 fresh seeds stopped on an undefined height.

The penalty evidence: IID against shifted, standard against importance-weighted

The advisor's questions, in his words: "Evidence on the penalty if it's constantly wrong/right. IW: is the weighting of the penalty correct or not. IID = low pen, but if IW has higher pen for IID then I need to see why. Does it always happen? Is this an exceptional case?" Here IID means test states drawn from the training law (the weighting test's "none" mix; coverage marks are judged on test steps outside the removed ball), shift the mild and strong current mixes, standard BCA with no weights and IW importance-weighted BCA. The full case list is PENALTY_EVIDENCE.md; every number is printed by penalty_cases.py, penalty_recompute.py or penalty_real_current.py.

IID against shifted: the standard penalty is not a direction signal

Standard BCA's penalty is the same number whether the test is IID or shifted, because it is read on the recorded training rows from a threshold fixed at the last refresh: the dose sits between 1.29 and 1.39 on every host, data quality and benchmark on record (110 readings), with a spread of at most 0.0041 across five different commands at the same states; stage 2's standard band differs by only +0.0003 to +0.0122 between the actor's harmful full-throttle command, its 80% cap and the recorded command (5 of 5 seeds); the band at the actor's unseen commands (past 80% throttle) is only 1.10 to 1.29 times its width at seen commands (25 of 25 seeds) while coverage there falls by 0.05 to 0.64. What drops under a shift is coverage, not the penalty: 0.889-0.940 per seed under IID to 0.797-0.873 under the strong shift, lower on 25 of 25 seeds for TD3+BC's critic, and 0.63-0.75 for CQL's. The one penalty that is right in direction is the harm switch's height: 1.41 to 6.02 where full throttle stalls, 0.04 to 0.77 where it is harmless, every stall height above every no-stall height (32 of 32 finite cases), because it reads held-out outcomes of the full-throttle group rather than where the states are.

Standard against IW: when is the weighted penalty higher under IID, and why

The consistent pattern. With the IID test declared exactly (weights of 1), IW never gives a higher penalty: it gives the same one, bit for bit, in every study (50 of 50 seed-hosts, 4 of 4 learners, 30 of 30 recomputed banks). With weights for a declared shift, IW's penalty is higher on every seed, by construction: the threshold 1.11-2.25 times on the gapped host and 1.08-1.86 on the full host (25 of 25 each), the dose +0.011 to +0.075 for TD3+BC on 25 of 25 and +0.125 to +0.156 for CQL on 10 of 10. The band is built for the declared test law, so this is intended; it restores coverage to at least 0.89 on 21 of 25 seeds under the strong shift and costs about 1 point of return on average without a shift, up to 2.7 points on a single seed (the capped pull on IID starts, outputs/shift_iw/explore/RESULTS.json).

The exceptional cases, each with its reproduction.

Case 7: classifier-estimated weights for the IID test move the threshold both ways.
The fitted slope on the current should be 0 and comes out −0.28 to +0.42 (mark W4, 25 seeds); fed to the threshold these weights move R by 0.913 (medium-expert seed 2) to 1.050 (medium-expert seed 4): higher on 14 of 25, lower on 9, equal on 2, beyond 5% on 2. The sign follows the sign of the fitted slope in 20 of the 23 moved cases, because a positive slope tilts the weights toward the high-current rows, where the scores are larger. R is one of the held-out scores, so a move of about 1% is one or two order-statistic steps. The −8.7% of medium-expert seed 2 (slope +0.00) stays unexplained; the Kish size of the recorded estimated weights was not stored. Classifier noise, not a mechanism of BCA. Reproduce: python docs/bca_mechanics/scripts/penalty_cases.py --root . --case 7.
Case 9: refusal when the effective number of held-out rows falls below about 29.
The credible quantile needs 950 of 1,000 draws to cross and a draw fails with probability 0.9^n. On record: every full-throttle group of 28 or fewer rows refused (18, 18, 19, 21, 22, 28 rows), every group of 30 or more certified, and at 29 rows one certified and one refused (the second 29-row refusal is the same random draw, because both runs tag the posterior with [20261015, 9700, seed, world, 1]). Three of the five fresh stalling seeds (10, 12, 13) had the switch on with an infinite height, and the approved code refused to build the arm. The IW arms with exact weights never refused a row (0 on 25 of 25 seeds, 0 on 10 of 10); the exploratory command-weighted band, whose effective bank fell to 0.3-21% of its rows, refused 24-100% of the actor's within-80% commands on 25 of 25 seeds. Reproduce: python docs/bca_mechanics/scripts/penalty_cases.py --root . --case 9, or subsample any recorded score set with M5_test.py check 2c.
Case 8 (consistent, by construction): strong-shift weights while training on IID rows.
The IW arm's band is calibrated for the strong test law, so the dose it reads on the IID training rows is higher than the standard arm's at every one of the 18 refreshes (seed 0, 90 of 90 chunks, a comparison of two trained runs), on the frozen band (25 of 25) and for CQL (10 of 10). Reproduce: --case 8.
Case 10 (control): no rise when the critic's error does not grow with the current.
ReBRAC's critic did not learn; its standard band already covered 0.90-0.96 under the shift, and the strong weights change its dose by −0.022 to +0.003. CQL's shuffled-weight placebo changes the dose by −0.008 to +0.017 against +0.125 to +0.156 with the real weights. Reproduce: --case 10.

The mechanism: why the weighted threshold is higher

Weights enter in one place, the threshold (M5); the scores, the error-size network and the unit are shared by the standard and weighted arms within a run (the four-learner stop rule S3 reproduced the standard threshold at every weighted refresh). penalty_recompute.py (pinned environment) takes the 30 recorded banks of held-out scores and changes one input at a time: weights of 1 reproduce the recorded threshold on 30 of 30 (case A); the heavier test atom alone adds 1.5% (case B); strong weights given to rows at random, which keep the smaller effective sample (Kish 0.35 n) but break the link between weight and score, add 9% on average (case C, range 0.81-1.51, above 1 in 522 of 600 draws), of which the rest beyond the test atom is the Bayesian margin growing from 9% to 17%; the same weights sorted onto the largest scores give the most the tilt can add, 2.91 (case D). penalty_real_current.py repeats the separation with the banks' own recorded currents on the 20 banks whose rows M3 rebuilt: at the weighting test's effective size (Kish 0.32, slope 9.4 on the recorded current range) the real-current threshold is 1.473 times the unweighted one (range 1.099-1.773), the same weights permuted across rows give 1.070 (1.023-1.143), so the tilt toward the high-current rows accounts for 1.375 (1.064-1.671), above the permuted control on 20 of 20 banks; at the mild and strong slopes (2 and 4) the real rise is 1.060 and 1.166 against 1.003 and 1.016 permuted. The rank correlation between a row's score and its current is only +0.004 to +0.147: the tilt loads the top of the current range, where the upper tail of the scores is heavier (M3, Part D: the 90% quantile of the scores is 1.3-1.6 times higher in the high-current third on 20 of 20 bands). In dose terms the sample-size part is about +0.01, the size of the four-learner shuffled placebo; the rest of the recorded 1.11-2.25 is the intended reweighting toward the rows where the critic is wrong by more.

Answer for the advisor. Standard BCA's penalty is the same number under IID and shift and cannot know where the data stop; coverage drops instead. The weighting is mechanically correct: with the IID test declared, IW is standard BCA to the last bit; with a declared shift its penalty is higher on every seed, mostly because the weights point the band at the high-current rows where the critic is wrong by more, and about 7-9% from the smaller effective sample. IW's penalty is higher under IID without a declared shift in two bounded cases, classifier noise of about plus or minus 5% and refusal below about 29 effective rows; neither is a bug in BCA's arithmetic.

What this does and does not show

1. This page verifies mechanics: that each component computes what its code says, reproduces its recorded numbers from the saved inputs, and behaves as the arithmetic predicts on synthetic data where the truth is known; the verdicts are about that, not about whether BCA raises return or prevents harm.

2. The return and harm results belong to the pre-registered tests and their own records: the weighting test's marks (specification version 5; outputs/shift_iw/v5/<quality>/report.json and summary.json on branch main), stage 2's marks on seeds 0-4 (outputs/shift/beyond-the-data/results-2026-10-13/ and results-2026-10-14/), step 1's go/no-go and step 2's go marks (outputs/shift/beyond-the-data/restructure/step1/results/results.json, step2_results/results.json), and the near-80 run's claims 1-4 (outputs/shift/beyond-the-data/near80/results-20261020T115246Z/files/looks/; claim 4 on fresh seeds 10-14 failed by rule because 3 of 5 stalling seeds stopped on an infinite height).

3. Where this page quotes those results (the lower edge's −13.0 against −13.2, the switched ramp's 87.4, step 2's net 102.9, the four-learner study's +6.54 for TD3+BC, shelved as not significant after the Holm adjustment), it quotes them with their own labels, exploratory on the seen seeds 0-4 in every case, and adds no new return claim.

4. Everything new here is exploratory or description only: the synthetic checks and the recomputations were designed on 20 October 2026 after all results were known, and the only thing fitted anywhere was M2's error-size network on synthetic rows; no critic, actor or band of a study was trained.

5. What the mechanics do settle: a fault in BCA's outcomes is not in the arithmetic of M1-M6, which reproduces bit for bit, but in what the band means, a band on the critic's one-step target that holds on average over recorded rows, and in the width's flatness across commands, which leaves the three width-reading uses (M7-M9) without leverage; the outcome-reading use (M10-M11) is the one whose results the pre-registered tests can speak to, and its open question is the height.

Glossary

BCA
Bayesian Conformal Aggregation, the project's method for putting an error band around an offline critic and turning the band into caution for the actor.
ThrusterChain
The project's simulated boat: the state is 13 numbers (the water current is the 11th), the command is 4 thruster throttles in [−1, 1]. The stalling world is the version in which a thruster's push falls past 80% throttle (the knee); the no-stall world is the version in which it does not.
Host, critic, actor, target
The host is the offline reinforcement-learning algorithm BCA is attached to (TD3+BC on ThrusterChain; TD3+BC, CQL, IQL and ReBRAC in the four-learner study). The critic Q(s, a) is its learned estimate of the return a command earns from a state (two heads, Q1 and Q2; q = min of the two). The actor is the controller being trained. The target y is the one-step value the host trains its critic toward: reward plus the discounted value the target copies give the next state.
Recorded row, training rows, held-out rows, evaluation rows
One step of a recorded log (state, command, reward, next state). A log of 1,000 episodes is split by episode into 500 training, 200 held-out calibration and 300 evaluation episodes; the held-out calibration rows ("the bank") are 5 rows from each of the 200 calibration episodes, about 800-850 after a removal.
Removal, the ball, the hidden throttle band, survivors
Rows hidden from training and from the held-out rows. The ball is the main setting's removal, the densest 15% of recorded commands; the hidden throttle band is the near-80 setting's extra removal, every command with a throttle from 70% to 90%; the random-rows setting removes as many random rows instead (the control). Survivors are the full-throttle commands outside the ball that stay in training.
Residual, error-size network, unit, score
The residual e = y − q is the critic's one-step error at a recorded row (M1). The error-size network η(s, a) predicts, per row, how large the residual should be as a multiple of the unit u, a running scale of the residual (M2). A score is |e| divided by u·η, a dimensionless size of one residual (M3).
Weights, test mass, Kish effective size
A weight w_j says how much held-out row j counts: how often its situation occurs at test time divided by how often it occurred in training. The test mass t is the weight of the row being certified. The Kish effective size (Σw)²/Σw² is how many equally weighted rows a weighted set is worth (M4).
Threshold, plain quantile, credible quantile, refusal, Bayesian margin
The threshold R is the score below which 90% of fresh scores should fall, with 95% credibility: the larger of the plain weighted 90% quantile λ̂ and the credible quantile λ_HPD, the 950th smallest of 1,000 crossings from random reweightings of the scores plus one test atom. R = +infinity is refusal, "cannot certify"; the Bayesian margin λ_HPD/λ̂ − 1 is the price of the credibility (M5).
Band, width, coverage, refresh
The band is q ± U with half-width U = R·u·η(s, a); a row is covered when its target lies inside; coverage of a group is the share covered, refused rows counting against it (M6). A refresh is the moment BCA freezes η and u and recomputes R on the held-out rows (update 10,000, then every 5,000 in co-training; once, after 20,000 fit steps, on a frozen critic); a chunk is the 5,000 updates between refreshes.
Dose, behavior-cloning term
The behavior-cloning term is the part of TD3+BC's actor loss that pulls the actor's command toward the recorded one; the dose m = 1 + 0.5·U/(U + u) is BCA's per-row multiplier on it (M7).
Lower edge, paired penalty, strength
The lower edge is Q1 minus k times the paired penalty, the positive part of the band's width at the actor's command minus its width at the recorded command (M9). Strength is how far a trained actor moved from the no-caution actor: the root-mean-square change of the command over 5,000 held-out states; rivals are matched to BCA's strength before returns are compared.
Harm switch, full-throttle group (tail), rest, q05, height, gap rule
The gap rule reads the kept training commands and finds the empty stretch of throttle above the data (t_lo to t_up). The full-throttle group is the survivors plus the held-out rows above t_lo; the rest is the other held-out rows. The switch runs M5's posterior on each group's one-sided overestimates and is on when q05, the 5% quantile of the difference of their crossings, exceeds 0.10 value units; the height is R_tail − R_rest, infinite when the tail cannot be certified (M10).
Ramp, switched ramp, arm, cloned actor, no caution
The ramp is a penalty on throttle, zero up to t_lo, rising to the height at t_up (M11). An arm is one trained variant evaluated under the same conditions as its rivals; the cloned actor, trained only to imitate the recorded commands, is every arm's starting point; "no caution" is the arm with no penalty. The hand-set range limit is the rival that simply caps the throttle at the recorded range.
Points, return units, situations
Points put the recording controller at 0 and the world's best scripted controller at 100; a return unit is the simulator's raw return, about 7.6 per point in the weighting test's worlds. The situations are four fixed sets of 1,000 test starts: recorded conditions, strong current, big waves, big kicks.
The studies on record
The main study (the ball removal; its accepted data and checks are "the gate", whose fixed-controller critic later studies reuse); stage 1 and stage 2 (the lower edge; stage 2's pre-registration is "version 6", so the version-6 band and arm are stage 2's standard band and lower-edge arm re-run inside the near-80 run); step 1 and step 2 (the harm switch and the ramp); the near-80 run (version 8: steps 1 and 2 on the main, near-80 and random-rows settings, seeds 0-4 and fresh seeds 10-14); the weighting test (specification version 5, five data qualities named after D4RL's data sets, random to expert, five seeds each; two hosts per seed, the gapped host trained after the ball's removal and the full host without); the four-learner study (TD3+BC, CQL, IQL, ReBRAC with standard and weighted BCA; seeds 0-4); the channel check (the band read at the actor's own command); the signal study (the dose on the D4RL benchmark hosts and a linear-quadratic control test bed); the toy notebooks.
Mark names
Pass/fail rules frozen before a run. The weighting test's marks M1-M3 are written WT-M1 (coverage with no shift), WT-M2 (the width tracks the exact critic error) and WT-M3 (dose mechanics) so that they are never confused with modules M1-M3; W0 (weights of 1 give the standard threshold bit for bit), W1-W4 (weighted coverage, unweighted coverage under the shift, refusal inside the ball, estimated against exact weights), R1-R2 (the dose arm's room and predicted return), L1-L3 (the lower edge). The four-learner study's stop rules S2, S3, S7; step 1's C1-C3; step 2's G1-G3 and A1-A3; the near-80 run's claims 1-4.
Pinned environment, Windows venv, WSL bridge
The pinned environment is Python 3.10.20, NumPy 2.2.6, JAX 0.6.2 on CPU, in the WSL clone at /home/user/bca, reached from Windows through wslrun.ps1; it is needed whenever a recomputed number must equal a recorded one to the last bit. The Windows venv (Python 3.14.2, NumPy 2.5.4, JAX 0.12.0) runs every test script; where the two draw the same random stream, the pages say so.
